question.text: Where a non-resident is eligible for benefits under a DTAA that India has with another country, the income is taxed under:

answer.text: Only the provisions of the Income Tax Act, irrespective of DTAA terms
Only the provisions of the DTAA, irrespective of the Income Tax Act
Either the relevant DTAA or the Income Tax Act, whichever is more beneficial to the taxpayer
The average of tax computed under both the Income Tax Act and the DTAA

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 217 and 228, where India has a DTAA with another country, a non-resident eligible for DTAA benefits is taxed under the relevant DTAA or the Income Tax Act, whichever is more beneficial. The Trap: Options A and B both pick one regime exclusively; neither matches the source rule. Option D fabricates an "average of both" approach with no basis in the workbook. Note: The "whichever is more beneficial" comparison is applied on the specific income head being taxed — for example, the DTAA rate on dividends or interest is compared with the corresponding IT Act rate.
